utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. No preliminaries were announced. Therefore, could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Radovanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it any better now? Is it any better now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I invite to you make that solemn declaration of which the text has been handed out to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Ms. Radovanovic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Ivetic. You find Mr. Ivetic to your left. Mr. Ivetic is a member of the Defence team of Mr. Mladic. Mr. Ivetic please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Professor.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name for the purposes of the record.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Svetlana Radovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Professor, I would like to call up 1D05357 which will be your CV but in the meantime could you please introduce yourself by giving a short resume of your work history?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I started my career in the bureau of statistics of the Republic of Serbia where I worked until the end of 1991. I ended my career there as head of the Department for Population Statistics. I took part in several preparations for, and processings of, the census and also, ex officio, I was in charge of a census. Also, I was an expert for methodology attached to an expert group formed by the federal bureau of statistics. In addition to that, I realised, organised a special census of part of Kosovo-Metohija under the auspices of the Serb Academy of Sciences and Arts. In 1992, I started working at the Institute of Social Sciences, the Centre for Demographic Research and I worked there until 1999 organising and carrying out certain projects related to the population. Also, I worked in the centre of peace of the United Nations, regarding these projects that had to do with different populations especially in Montenegro. In 1999, I started working at the Faculty of Geography of the University of Belgrade and I stayed there until 2014. In this CV of mine there is something missing namely that piece of information. It says that I worked there until 2013 but simply I handed in this CV early on. But in 2014, in July, I retired. I retired as head of the Department for Demographics at the Faculty of Geography. I worked on many scientific projects and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I invite you to slow down so that the interpreters can catch all your words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that nothing will be missed. Please proceed. You said you worked on many scientific projects. And then. Could you please resume from there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Projects organised by the Faculty of Geography, projects organised by other institutions and as I said in July I retired as head of Department for Demographics at the Faculty of Geography. I held different posts there. I was also deputy dean for finance, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what subjects you taught while at university?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: As regards undergraduate studies, as well as masters studies and doctoral studies, I taught several subjects. Introduction to demography, statistics of population, ethno-demography, methods of demographic analysis, geopolitics and population.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we look at the second page in both languages of your CV in the section, "Other Professional Activities", which we now have on the screen, you have reflected here that you have been an expert before the ICTY. Can you please tell us how many times and which cases you appeared in?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I testified in the trial that dealt with the siege of Sarajevo. I think it was General Galic's trial. Also, I testified about ethnical structure and ethnical changes in Samac at the Blagojevic, et al trial. Then at the Jadranko Prlic et al trial, and I guess I haven't forgotten anything. I think it was five trials that I testified at and I cannot remember the fifth one now. Oh, yes. Popovic. Popovic. Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Apart from the date of your retirement, do you believe this curriculum vitae to be complete and accurate?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would tender 1D05357 as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence, under number, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 1D05357 receives exhibit number D1210, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, as I said, is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Professor, you have prepared a written report for this case. At this time I would call up 1D05356. And I have a hard copy here if you need it.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have my own copy, but if you wish, you can give me that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's usual that the parties provide the copies you can consult because no one has inspected your copy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So would you please - whatever you have brought you not consult it without having asked permission to do so and you'll be provided with whatever you say you need.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can open to the first page in both -- I guess page 2 in e-court in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you tell us what was the task or assignment that you received for purposes of this case, the Mladic case.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was supposed to see how well founded the information is, the information presented in the expert report of the Prosecution to look at all the sources they used, to give my comment regarding these sources, to see whether they applied methodology that is used in the science of demographics and statistics, to assess the results that they obtained and to indicate many methodological problems that they have, if any, and also to give my own assessment of the report that they made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just seek verification of the translation. We received as the translation of what you said that you were invited to assess the results that they have obtained and to indicate many methodological problems that they have.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I was thinking, that it would be "any" rather than "many." Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you've identified the expert report of the Prosecution. Was your task relating to one or more of the Prosecution experts?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Several of them. Simply because expert analyses were made by several experts, not only one. One expert analysis that has to do with ethnic changes was done by Dr. Ewa Tabeau, one expert. However, at the end of her report, she also says that she was assisted by certain people.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And if we can turn to page 3 in both languages. Starting towards the bottom of the page, you begin listing reports analysed and it goes on to the next page. And if we could turn to page 5 in both languages, we come to the end of that list at 21 items. And then on that fifth page you also list 15 data sources analysed. Did you have occasion to review any additional materials, apart from that which you have listed here, for purposes of doing your review and drafting your report?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: All the materials that were accessible and that I deemed could be of significance when I reviewed the reports of the Prosecution experts, I took a look at all of that. I also looked at the data sources that are partly contained in the demographics office of the OTP, but also I looked at sources that I did not see at the demographics office of the OTP. That is to say, I reviewed everything that was made accessible to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just to we are clear about your testimony today, both your testimony today and your report do not deal with or analyse Dr. Tabeau's new report on Tomasica. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I still have -- it's not entirely clear to me. You said, "All the materials that were accessible and that I deemed could be of significance when I reviewed the reports, I took a look at all that." Now, you have listed the 21 reports you analysed. You have given 15 data sources. What other materials or is that all that you have looked at; and, if not, could you tell us what other material you looked at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is all that I studied meticulously. But I also reviewed some other material that has to do with statistics, say, statistics, recent statistics of Bosnia-Herzegovina that I had occasion to see so that I could see whether they could be used as such or not. I also reviewed, earlier on when I was in the demographics department, some materials that might pertain to this. But now they were not accessible to me. So I could not mention them in this list --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... two questions: First of all, do we find a references to those sources you are now telling us you consulted? That's the first question: Do we find that in footnotes, or that I found that here or I found that there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I provide footnotes for everything that I refer to. As for sources that I consulted apart from this and that I decided I would not use, I did not mention them, and there is no explanation or footnote regarding them. Each and every source, if I'm quoting something, or if I am referring to something, it is stated where it was taken from, from which report, from which book, from which publication, what the page is, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... so every material you've used, you have considered, we find it referenced in the -- either in the text or in the footnotes. Second question is: You said I had no access to certain materials. Did you try to find access? Because it's always of some concern to the Chamber if experts say, We couldn't look at it because we didn't have it. Because this Chamber often can assist in giving access to or getting access to certain sources. What is it exactly that you could not have access to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked the Defence to make it possible for me to go to the demographics office of the Office of the Prosecutor to take a look at the materials used. For example, in 2004, 2005, I did have some insight, but it's been a while, so I thought that I should take a look, again, at some of these sources and some of these materials that were used by Prosecution experts. As far as I know, the Prosecution did provide its consent. However, the Registry said that the demographics office was closed right now, if my understanding is correct, that they first have to discuss it with Dr. Tabeau, that I should say what it is that I want to see and that they would notify me when I could come, if at all. To this day, I haven't heard from them and perhaps the Defence knows better than I do what all of this is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you told them what you wanted to see? Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I mentioned all the sources that I wished to look at. For example, I never saw --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... at this moment, I'm not that much interested in the details. Rather, in how it went.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Uh-uh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can assist further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, because the Chamber, have we missed something that there was something that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The Prosecution and the Defence have not had any problems in regard to this. We've co-operated fully. The Registry has not agreed to authorise that trip yet for Ms. Radovanovic and her assistants who would be performing that work. Still in the process of trying to arrange that for the Tomasica part of the case since this expert has only recently been appointed as an expert for that portion of the case, which we sought sometime ago, but only I think it was last week or the week before has been appointed by the Registry for that function.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand that the only portions you had no access to is the Tomasica materials? Or.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I should ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: She has had not access since 2007 to any of the materials from the OTP's demographic database.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when was the request made? Because what you're telling us that at this moment that Prosecution was not opposing but the Registry blocked, more of less, or frustrated access to materials which are apparently relevant. When was the request made to have access to that material, so when was it that the Registrar or the Registry blocked, more or less access.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't say blocked access. I'm talking about funding which are two entirely different matters. They have invited the Defence and the experts to basically go out of their own pocket to perform this work. That most recent correspondence as to that was approximately, I think, three weeks ago. The request having been made months before for the -- specifically -- that part was specifically dealing with Tomasica matter, once we did receive some additional hours for her to be appointed as an expert for Tomasica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- Tomasica which is a -- I would say is a separate issue. Was there any hindrance in getting access to all the non-Tomasica materials? The witness says, Well, I had no access to materials, but Tomasica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We have no funding. I don't know how else I can explain to Your Honours. The Prosecution gave their consent, I believe, both times and we didn't have funding. And we're still trying to arrange funding for the expert and her assistants to come here and use the facilities that the Office of the Prosecutor has offered for that matter, and we're hoping to get that resolved, and then to allow her to have access to do whatever she needs to do to verify whether any findings need be to modified based upon having access to that material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When was a request for funding made in relation to the non-Tomasica material?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, standing here on my feet I do not know. It's been an ongoing process so I cannot -- I cannot guess and mislead the Court as to when the original request was made. I can only say that the most recent request was made approximately, I think, three or four months ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With the appointment of the expert coming in the last week or two and with the issue of funding for the assistants of the expert's also still in limbo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now the report was filed - let me just have a look - in March 2015. Do I understand that -- were there any requests for further funding made before March 2015 well, before that because then the report apparently was concluded which is -- you understand that the Chamber wants to know in detail what are the reasons that there may be insufficient materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Relying upon my memory and my memory alone, the original request to review the documents came during the Prosecution's case in-chief, at which time the Prosecution said that they did not have an objection. And I think that was sometime in late 2014 when Ms. Tabeau testified the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because that apparently is mixed up now and then. Was that a request to also have the necessary funding or was it a request to have access to the materials irrespective of any funding? Because in the beginning I understood the testimony, to some extent, to be that the Registrar had frustrated or blocked access to the materials. Whereas now it turns out that it's at least also a financial matter, and asking further details about when requests for funding were made and when requests for access were made, that the request for funding you mentioned is three, four months, four months ago, which is after the report had been submitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That was a renewed request because of the Tomasica case reopening, and then we sought to have the expert qualified to provide assistance for the Tomasica part of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the reason why I asked for the non-Tomasica materials. Because it's -- it's -- I understand that Tomasica is still to be worked on. It's not part of this report. So, therefore, I'm wondering what frustrated access to any materials for the report as it is before us now: Is that a lack of co-operation by the Registry; and, if so, is a matter of funding, or is it a matter of we have closed the department, therefore you can't have access. These the questions the Chamber would very clearly distinguish and not mix them up. Do you have any further information, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I do. I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My recollection is that originally there was a concern that the department had to be opened up, but the Prosecution agreed to do that and the Prosecution consented to having the expert and the assistant who I think had assisted here on the prior trip to the demography unit years ago. And it's an issue of funding. The funds for the work of Ms. Radovanovic were expended in full and we did not have additional hours available. We've been -- the issue the funding with the Registry has been an ongoing matter for many experts, so that's why it's a little bit difficult for me to recall every single detail since the funding for experts for the Defence always an issue. And it's one that we have made dealings both written, oral, and otherwise with the Registry and it's a painstaking process. And like I said we finally were able to get some additional -- to get Ms. Radovanovic appointed for additional hours to look at Tomasica and we're trying to get approval for her assistants and her to come and to review the material at the Demographic Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, at this moment we have no details about neither funding or access in the earlier stages when the additional funding and additional access for Tomasica were not playing a role.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I cannot provide those details, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. File. Do you have any further comment on the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: In case it would be of assistance, I can give you some further details on the request for access to the demographic databases in the OTP. The request that I'm aware of was received on the 14th of July of this year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that for Tomasica or was that for the -- because by then, the report had been produced already. Is there any earlier request for access?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'm not aware of an earlier request for access and that request did not specify Tomasica it was just for access to the demographic database. And we responded on the 16th, I believe, of July offering a series of dates that would be available between the 27th of July and the 7th of August, or any time in September, starting from the 7th of September. And that's where we left our correspondence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now -- and now I'm addressing the witness. You said that you heard that the department was closed and that was a problem. Are you talking about the time between the 7th of August and September, or are you talking about any earlier period when the demographic department was closed temporarily or permanently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about an earlier period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what period was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the moment when I was negotiating and hiring for the report that we will be discussing today, I talked to the lawyers and told them that it would be good for me to have access and review the material that I know only in part, and there's one database that I don't know at all. And as far as I'm informed, a request has been made for me to gain access and a response was given, but I don't have it here, but nobody would mind. But because the demographics office is currently closed, I have to specify what I want to see so that Dr. Tabeau could get on that case and give me access to these databases. After that, I didn't receive any more answers from anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, you said: "And as far as I'm informed a request has been made to gain access and a response was given but I don't have it here but nobody would mind." When was that? Was that this year? Was that one year ago? Two years ago? Five years ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was certainly last year, before I finished my expert report relating to the subject we will be discussing today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. And you say because the demographic office is currently closed. Are you also now referring to last year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can't be 100 per cent sure but it was certainly before I submitted my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then you said: "I have to specify what I want to see so that Dr. Tabeau could get on that case and give me access to these databases." When did you inform Dr. Tabeau about what you wanted to see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never informed Dr. Tabeau directly. I make a request and pass it on to the lawyers, and they do the rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I earlier raised this issue, but I have to find it. One... let me see where ... One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could you switch off your microphone in the meantime. The interpreters asked for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the witness earlier said that when I asked whether she had informed - and I think I said "them" - I may have had on my mind the Demographic Unit or the Registry, but the witness then said: "I mentioned all the" -- let me just ... "sources that I wished to look at." Did you mention that to the Defence? Is that how I have to understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure I understood you, but the procedure is as follows. If I want to review --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... no, I'd rather deal with it on the basis of your testimony until now. You said as far as you knew, the Prosecution had provided its consent. Registry said demographic office was closed right now. And that if your understanding is correct, they first have to discuss it with Dr. Tabeau and that you should say what it is that you wanted to see and that they would notify me when I could come, if at all. Now, you said to this day, I haven't heard from them and perhaps the Defence knows better than I do what all of this is about. And then I asked you, and you told them what you wanted to see. And you said, yes, I mentioned all the sources that I wished to look at. To whom did you mention them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems we didn't understand each other well. I write a request for the law firm for which I'm currently working. Through them, I make all the requests. I never have direct contact with experts, with the Registry, with anybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you specify to the Defence what materials you wanted to see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I write to the Defence, specifying which materials I need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has that been -- and now I'm addressing you, Mr. Ivetic. Has that been relayed to Dr. Tabeau?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I cannot have access with Dr. Tabeau. We're waiting for approval of the mission to then make arrangements with the OTP, which was the way that it was left, I believe by Mr. Tieger saying, let us know what you need, we'll make it available, free computers et cetera. We're all waiting for the mission to be, shall we say, funded. I do have additional information as to the original request that was in 2013, as I found the e-mail from Mr. McCloskey talking about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, Mr. Ivetic, did you in way or another relay the list of what Ms. Radovanovic wanted to see so that Dr. Tabeau would know about, because she understood that the answer by the Registry had been, tell us what you need and then we'll see what happens. So my question simply is - and there may be good or bad reasons for it - has the request to see certain materials, has that been, in one way or another, been sent to Dr. Tabeau?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It has been sent to the Prosecution with the response that we also, when we got closer to the date of visit, specify with more detail. Now I do not send things directly to Dr. Tabeau. That's the problem with -- that I have with the question. Now I can read to you the e-mail from October 28th with Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, perhaps -- yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Which says: "Yes, that is why I asked. We know her and she has had access before which went off with no problem. As you know, Ewa no longer works here, so logistically it won't be as easy as it was before, but Max is in the best position to set this up and she will be in touch soon." And so the original discussions were in October of 2013 which is why they're not so fresh in my memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I have before me, Mr. President, the most recent exchange of information to which Mr. Ivetic referred, and that entailed a request by the Defence: "Dear colleagues, I hereby convey to you the request of our demographic expert, Professor Radovanovic, to permit her to gain access to the demographic databases, et cetera. Please apprise us as soon as possible whether the Office of the Prosecutor consents, under what terms that access would be, what time-frame or potential dates would be available, et cetera." That was sent on the 14th of July of this year and on the 17th of July we responded that we consent, that we can set up computers for Professor Radovanovic and her two assistants, and make arrangements for them to have access to the requested sources, and database. And towards that end we asked to be advised of the following: As precisely as possible the number of days that the professor and her assistants would require access, how many computers would be needed, whether those computers needed to be connected with each other through a local network, and a list of specific sources they wished to consult. And then we advised of available dates as related by Mr. File earlier. And indicated we would ask for approximately one week notice in order to make the -- to organise access and set up the computers for any particular set of dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I think we should leave it to that at this very moment. But, of course, we'll understand, Mr. Ivetic, that it's of some concern to the Chamber that an expert here says, Well, I didn't have the necessary material to -- but let's proceed and the Chamber may want to follow up this in more detail and to know exactly what was done when and with what kinds of phrasing it was done. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put one additional question to Mr. Tieger. You said you responded on 17th of July, consenting and giving more details about the way it should be conducted. Did you receive an additional letter from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. Thank you. Or Your Honour, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we all were once were Presiding Judges so, therefore, it's totally appropriately to now and then call my colleagues Mr. President as well. Mr. Ivetic, let's move on but we may want to pay attention to this procedural aspect later. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Professor, can you explain for us, very briefly, the type of methodology that you used when drafting your report; that is to say, how did you set about analysing the work of the Prosecution experts.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I applied the usual methodological procedure for this kind of analysis. I first gathered all the sources of information that are relevant to this analysis, I looked at all the databases that I had access to, all the findings that I had related to these databases, then I grouped these reports by topic and the literature and the data that I have, and then I made an analysis and made some causal conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you have an opinion as to whether the type of review and reporting undertaken by the Prosecution experts adheres to the standards normally used in the science of demography?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that the reports provided by the Prosecution experts are a construction. They do not apply the scientific methodology used in demographics and statistics. Instead, they use a model based on a methodology that the Prosecution experts themselves call uniform methodology. That methodology is adjusted to its own research and is not applied in any other scientific research, only in the demographics office of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask again whether there may be ... you said the Prosecution experts themselves call it a uniform methodology. I think I read in the report that you were talking about a unique methodology. Is that what you wanted to refer to or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unique, they call it unique. At least that's the translation I get in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... yes. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to review your report prior to today in its entirety to make sure that everything is correctly noted in the Serbian original of the same?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I looked at them. There is maybe a small problem with the footnotes, especially in the translation into English, but I believe all the footnotes were recorded properly. When I says there is a problem, I don't mean that anybody intentionally did it, but the number of pages of the report in Serbian and in English do not coincide.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you stand behind everything that is written in your report?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would ask for the report, 1D05356, to be marked for identification at this time since we have been alerted to some issues of the English translation in the introduction and as Your Honours can see on the screen, for instance, there's the wrong date even though the cover page of the English has the same date as -- in the original. This page has a different date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes apart from that, I think usually admission is --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- done only at the end of the examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number under which this report would be MFI would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 1D05356 receives exhibit number D1211, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we can turn to page 15 in both languages of your report. And while we wait for that, you have referred to unique methodology used by the Prosecution experts. Could you tell us how that -- what that means. How does that -- how does that relate to the methodology one would expect for this time of work?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Brunborg explained in one of his works, elaborating on the methodology they applied, he called it a unique methodology, and Dr. Tabeau repeated that several times. By unique methodology, they understand a modified scientific methodology. They modified it in a way that is scientifically and technically inadmissible. That modification can indeed, be called unique but it has no base in science. It is a methodology that makes it possible for a statistician to target certain statistical data, and I show that in my analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you first explain for us what it is you mean when you say that they could target their data? And I think it's on this page in the first paragraph you talk about targeted statistical findings. So what do you mean when you say "targeted statistic findings"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic I would like to first understand the beginning of the answer of the witness. You said by unique methodology, they understand a modified scientific methodology, so I do understand that they deviated from what is standard and called that unique. You say they modified it in a way that ask scientifically and technically inadmissible. Could you tell us what exactly they changed so that we know what you mean by scientifically and technically inadmissible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They modified but they don't explain. They present it as if it were the real methodology. And from that I conclude that they are making a methodological patent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Even if they don't explain it, what did they change without explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. First of all, they don't apply the method of matching in a standard statistical way, they invent new definitions that do not exist. They invent and present results in a way that is, to put it mildly, comparing apples and oranges. They compare completely different groups to make conclusions. They show certain parameters that are statistically and demographically groundless and they used them to explain demographic phenomena.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is all very abstract. Could you point at us what they are doing, where are they, as you said, comparing apples and oranges. In order for us to understand, it is not purely your judgement on it but we'd like to understand what exactly it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we plan on going through each and every single one of those. We're still at the introductory phase of the expertise now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I still want to understand these kind of things, and if that's just the introduction, Mr. Ivetic, then I would suggest that you go first through that. Because you started asking further details about targeted statistical findings, whereas I thought the previous part of the answer was in need of some further elaboration as well. But if you think that it would be good to do it this way, then please proceed, but be aware that it raises already many questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like ask the witness to clarify one sentence. A minute ago you said it is a methodology that makes it possible -- as I read it in the transcript, for a statistician to target certain statistical data and I note that in my analysis. Did you say it made it impossible or possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The method -- with the method they are using, it's possible, with a modified method of matching. And I was intending to show you all this. If you give 71 criteria, you can match whatever you please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That means --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For example, that's just one instances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if you said possible or impossible. I understand you now that you said it is a methodology that makes it possible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's possible to target.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that's what I wanted to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I think it's time for the break. Ms. Radovanovic, we'll take a break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes because we'll resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Professor, on page 15 of your report, the last paragraph, that starts: "The Prosecution experts know that the 'unique methodology' has no real scientific and professional foundation so they just to justify it with an incredible explanation that 'there exists as well methodological limitations in court analysis, observed counts are the most favourable type of statistics, demographic rates, ratio, probabilities and other relative measures of intensity of death or missing or migration will already be questioned and complex statistical estimates and results of statistical modelling and extrapolation are always strongly challenged or totally neglected.'" Now, the quote you have is from Dr. Tabeau. In preparing your expertise and report, did you experience any methodological limitations of the type described by Dr. Tabeau?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I know for sure that there aren't any methodological limitations for court analyses and other analyses. There are scientific or non-scientific analyses. Now for what purpose or occasion they were prepared for, that has nothing to do with any of this, as far as I know, and as far as I know within my own profession that court analyses are prepared using some different methodology in which one should not express probability and so on. So there is no such thing as court analyses. Actually, there are court analyses, but there is not some kind of a border between court analyses and other types of analysis, on the other hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could return to the first paragraph, I'd ask that we'd -- not had an answer. You used a term "targeted statistical findings" in relation to the methodology, the unique methodology of the Prosecution. Can you explain for us what it is you mean when you use the words "targeted statistical findings."

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: If you use certain methods and you do not use them the way they are actually used in scientific analysis, if you modify them, rather, then precisely due to that modification, you expect, in advance, to get something that suits you and, as I've already said, the modified method of matching used by the OTP experts is an excellent example of that. If you cannot apply a definition that is customary and that is used in science and the demographic science if you have to, if I can put it that way, invent a new definition or rather invent a name for something without explaining what this new name means and what this new definition means, then, again, by adjusting the definition that does not exist in demographic science, you are actually paving the way for yourself to declare something that you have done to be scientific in some way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you say if you change the definitions, we'd like to go to the concrete - I don't know whether you are going to ask the witness where definitions are changed, how they are challenged and what the impact is. Because, until now it's all abstract. Similarly, you in your report, as it was quoted by Mr. Ivetic, you are apparently dealing or are you quoting from a report of 2009, which is not in evidence, as far as I'm aware of, or is it, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe it is not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And therefore we don't know the context. We don't know what it's all about. It's just a quote of five, six lines, also rather abstract. So therefore what we'd like to know is how this all impacts, how this finds its way into the reports that are in evidence and how that impacts on findings and what you would consider to be the proper findings instead of what you are criticizing. Please proceed. Let's get to understand ... I leave it to Mr. Ivetic to put further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, with a difficult field like demography we need to first understand the basic premises before going to specific examples. Unless Your Honour has a degree, I don't. And this is how I intend to do it to understand and appreciate it, and so that's how I feel it's most helpful, to go through and to establish these foundations, as you will, and then go to the application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If they are too abstract we are not even, in the early stages to link them to what we find in the report and to follow the critics to the criticism to that report. But I leave it again in your hands, but I just wanted to express clearly again what we finally would like to understand and -- because we finally have to decide on who's giving -- we have to weigh this evidence, the evidence of this witness against the evidence of Ms. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm confused now, because I have been citing exactly to where she talks about in her report, asking her to explain about it. I don't know how can I link her testimony to her report any better than that. I say the page number, I read from her report, and I ask her to comment upon that. There's no other method I can use to link it to hear report better. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean to link it to the reports which are reviewed by this witness, not in the report here because we see that as a quote from something that was apparently published in 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Talking about her work for the Tribunal, yes. By Dr. Tabeau, the Prosecution expert. It's 1D5340.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... all very much in the abstract. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn to page 16 of your report in both languages and in both languages, just down a few lines from the top, and you are again quoting Dr. Tabeau's 2009 publication where she said: "Trial Chambers are not experts in the statistical methodology, and explaining difficult methods does not work well in courtrooms, the result of presenting complicated calculations as part of expert reports and testimonies usually is less successful than simple results obtained from reliable and well-documented sources." What is your understanding of this method that Dr. Tabeau is talking about? Would you agree that these affect what you can present to courts?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's not a method. This is the position of Dr. Tabeau. She thinks that the Trial Chamber are not experts in statistics, which is a fact, but I cannot believe that if you are an expert in a particular field, you cannot explain that thing to the Trial Chamber so that they can understand. So I disagree with that position, and I believe that it is absolutely wrong, regardless of the field involved. If someone who is knowledgeable in his own profession, then he or she can always give an answer to any question put by the Trial Chamber, so I think this position is totally wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Next I want to look at two things by Dr. Brunborg before we go to the specifics. Now in relation to Dr. Brunborg at the bottom of the same page in your report, we have the quotation from his publication: "Demographers are trained to be very critical towards data and methods and to present and discuss their weaknesses. In a report presented to a court such issues should not play such a major role in the presentation such as to overshadow the major findings." Is Dr. Brunborg's depiction of how demographers are to present things to a court in accord with the field of demography as you and others in the same field know it?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I absolutely disagree with this position as well. I believe that it is important for the Trial Chamber and how to understand the methodology used by someone. It's not for demographers to discuss the methodology only amongst themselves so the methodology applied in any analysis, if the Trial Chamber does not understand it, it is absurd for us to discuss it between and among ourselves as experts in a particular field. So I don't think that such questions do not play a major role. I think the methodological questions play a very, very important role. Because to present one's main findings and not to explain the way in which you arrived at these major findings and not to confirm that you used a methodology that is based on scientific methodology is pointless. If I'm supposed to present findings without explaining my methodology, then you're supposed to take my word for something and in sciences no one takes anyone's word for anything. You have to have proof, of course, depending on the science that you work in, so I disagree with the position of Dr. Brunborg, just like I disagreed with Dr. Tabeau's position.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What do you consider is the appropriate way of dealing with weaknesses in one's own methodology and findings in a demographic sense when presenting evidence before a court?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think it is very important to be honest, vis-à-vis one's own science. I think it is important to abide by scientific methods and that you should confirm everything that you arrived at, scientifically, methodologically. I think that ethics is an integral part of science, irrespective of all the education and training you've had. Science is a painstaking effort but there can be no science without ethnics. That is to say, a demographer who receives certain material in order to work on an analysis, has to be absolutely honest in assessing each and every step that you're supposed to take in order to finalize a paper. Also, I believe that it is important to present the data that is acceptable, that is reliable, at least minimally reliable. Although we may have some idea of that not being that convincing, but for -- if you say that something is reliable and if you used a proper methodology then you can say, yes, this is what I could establish while applying scientific methodology. Now whether there is something else or whether there is not anything else, that's a different matter. You cannot just assume that this other thing, if scientific methodology was not applied, can be justified by reliable results.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you believe that the reports authored by Dr. Brunborg and Dr. Tabeau and entered into evidence in this case honestly discuss the weakness of their methods and findings?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this word honest, doesn't sound right to me at this point in time; [B/C/S spoken] posteno. If view of the schooling they've had, the knowledge that they have, the experience they have on the basis of their CV, they could have approached this job in a completely different way, methodologically proper. And they could stand by their results, and without any problems they could explain that and they could claim that these data are relatively reliable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, if I -- you would allow me to just put one question in between. Ms. Radovanovic, did you read the testimony of the expert witnesses in this case? I mean, the demographic expert witness. It was Dr. Tabeau mainly who testified. Did you read the testimony as given in this Court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't read it in this case. In the previous cases, yes. But there are no transcripts in Serbian in this case. However, I listened to all the testimony, the video footage, of Dr. Brunborg and Dr. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Also in this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this case. This case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yeah, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now if we take a look at the next part of the same paragraph, you highlight Dr. Brunborg where he said: "The critical question is how -- is thus how many victims must be established to convict someone of genocide." First of all, do you consider such a question as an appropriate starting premise for one to undertake when engaged in demographic or statistical analysis?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I don't know who put this key question. Was it put by an expert demographer or was it somebody else who put this key question? At any rate, a key question cannot be a number that has to be established. If you have as your task a number that has to be established, then you have to try to find your way, do this and that, just try to get to that figure. But the key question is the reliability of the results obtained, not a number, a figure, that has to be established.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, the article that you cite to by Dr. Brunborg is called: Accounting for Genocide: How Many were Killed in Srebrenica? What is the commonly accepted definition of genocide that is used in the practice of professional demography?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: In scientific demography, there is no definition of genocide. When a demographer - if he starts dealing with such analysis at all - then he or she uses definitions of the UN. I'm not saying that there are not any other definitions. I assume that at this Court there is also a definition of genocide. As an author, this person can use that definition as well. However, from a professionally honest point of view, then one should put a footnote and say: Genocide denotes such and such a thing as stated by the Court or the UN or an author who dealt with this matter. So a demographer does not have a definition of genocide. However, since demography is a multi-faceted science, you can use all scientific findings and all professional findings from other fields, from other sciences. However, as I said you have to have professional integrity and say that is that. And this is what I mean by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the last part from here that I want to talk about is the very next citation again from Dr. Brunborg: "The ICTY genocide criteria: Acts committed with the intent to destroy, in whole or" --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And we have to go to the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "... in part, a national, ethnical, racial or religious group." And then you continue to quote Dr. Brunborg that the ICTY definition does not state, however" -- and we have to go to the next page in Serbian: "... the number or proportion inquired for a genocide charge. It is generally assumed that the number or proportion needs to be significant." What is your opinion or comment as to the description of Dr. Brunborg of the assumed number -- assume that the number of proportion needs to be significant in a demographic sense?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, I believe it is improper, because I say this again, the criteria of the Court, the international Court, the ICTY, have to be met. That is not a criterion. That's a definition. Then it is proper to say the criteria are such and such. If a person believes that numbers are criteria and are assumed to be important, now, is this Dr. Brunborg's finding, is this his conclusion? And no one is cited here so I believe that this is his general position that he established at the very outset of his paper and that that was, if I can put it that way, his guide-line in drafting his report, from the very outset up until this conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, apart from the statements of Dr. Tabeau and Dr. Brunborg talking about the work that they did at the Tribunal, did you find specific fault --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it any better now? Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's start from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now apart from these statements by Dr. Tabeau and Dr. Brunborg talking about the work they did at this Tribunal, did you find specific faults with the actual work product as submitted to the Tribunal which you believed to be outside the standards of scientific demography? If you could now list for us some of the -- some of these.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: There are shortcomings that are primarily methodological problems. A methodological problem is when you are doing a demographic expert report without defining precisely the area that you are working on. It's also a methodological problem if you are manipulating that area. If there is no definition of that area, you can stretch it and shrink it. Srebrenica is a typical example. There is not a single report that gives a definition of what the experts understand by Srebrenica. They call it enclave one moment, then they call it a demilitarised territory, then they represent Srebrenica as an area of 15 municipalities and some settlements which are not actually Srebrenica-related populated areas, and they include even four municipalities of western Serbia, Valjevo, Loznica, Bajina Basta, and Ljim. Ljig - correction. And they gather data about everything they found in those municipalities on a particular date, but when they represent data related to Srebrenica, they show it for five municipalities. If they had defined precisely what they understand by Srebrenica, there would be no problem, but they have to know, especially when they are representing various statistical parameters, the exact population number, and they have to work with the particular number because methodology says that the groups have to be comparable. The area you are working on has to be specified. That's one of the most important problems. The lack of definition of a particular territory. In the ethnic structure of the population in migrations, the problem is less serious, but, again, it is not explained to which area it pertains. Dr. Tabeau presents her data relative to the new administrative division which was established in Bosnia-Herzegovina after 1995, that is to say, after the Dayton Accords, while everything that happened and that is encompassed by the indictment happened - and I include also the census - happened in an area with a different administrative division. This change between the old and the new is significant in as far as it's explained nowhere why you represent Bosnia now as Republika Srpska and the Federation and not the old Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Why not explain, if you are using the new administrative division, which number of the population you omitted from the new settlements? Dr. Tabeau says "a small number." In statistics there is no such thing as a small number. You can say, one, five, ten. I think that it is a kind of misrepresentation, precisely because the Prosecution experts think it insignificant. They say Srebrenica victims, but, to me, it's not defined, and they didn't define anywhere showing the ethnic structure why you are using the new administrative division. I don't think it's professionally proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As you know, we'll get to pointing to the specific findings of the experts. Could you now briefly detail for us apart from the flaws you believe as to the naming of the territory and the territory used for various studies, what other types of deficiencies did you note from the reports of the Prosecution experts? And then we'll go through each one of them one by one with looking at the actual material.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: They never provided anywhere the correct assessment of the data. They put in a piece of information here and there, but the assessment they give at the end is not defined. They say regardless of the shortcomings, these results are reliable. Then they deal with the broad concept of something without defining what the broad context is, except saying that they take information for 1991 and 1997, in the case of Dr. Tabeau, when they are showing forced migrations. The broad context doesn't mean taking two years or two sources that exist. A broad context means explaining what happened between 1991 and 1998, and what could have happened demographically. So this broad context is not correct. It doesn't mean dealing with what exists and calling that broad contexts. For instance, Dr. Tabeau says that the broad context became an imperative at the ICTY, but she never explains who imposed that imperative. Were they told: You have to take the broad context or they decided themselves that, since there are no other sources, they deal with the broad context.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Professor, if I can ask you to clarify one thing. In the scientific demography, the field of scientific demography, how -- what is -- or how is a source graded or assessed, and in that answer if you could please explain what are statistics of error?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: You assess a source by looking at what it contains and how many errors there are in that source. In serious scientific studies, what is tolerated is the so-called statistical error, which ranges from 2 to 5 per cent. All, all sources used by the Prosecution experts have a much higher statistical error than is acceptable in science. For instance, the Red Cross at the time when I checked it, did not have 35 per cent of information on years of birth. In the latest report, Dr. Brunborg says that 25 percent is now lacking. So, in the meantime, they managed to increase it by 7 or 8 per cent. There is also lacking information about the place of disappearance, but they say with smaller errors. But they don't define smaller. Is it 7, 10 or 50? And then they say we made corrections on hundreds of thousands of names. Hundreds of thousands out of which number? So it's very approximate. Scientifically, you have to grade every source statistically, give it a quality assessment. You can't just say there are many blanks and gaps but generally the source is good, electoral lists and the census have approximately the same data. That's not good enough. It's not a serious way to deal with this, statistically, demographically. There is no such assessment, there are no corrections in any of the reports I looked at. Corrections were made, perhaps, to the first expert reports, but they ignore such an important thing. When grading a source, you can't just say it lacks 35 per cent of this particular information, but generally it's good. And also they say all together with the Red Cross information, when combined, these two sources appear good. No, that's not the way it's done.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Doctor, what comment do you have as to the manner in which the information from the Bosnian Ministry of Defence was utilised in the reports authorised by the Prosecution experts and introduced into evidence?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: One of the really major methodological problems is a very selective choice of sources. utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Matching is a standard statistical method that is applied far more broadly than demography or statistics as such. Perhaps the most evident example of what matching is, the fact that every day we carry out some kind of matching. Everybody who has a pin card and uses it in a cash dispenser, that person has to provide that pin code, right, so then that pin code is typed in and then it is matched to your details there at the bank, and if you have money on your account, you are given money, and, if not, you don't get any money. You cannot change that money without the approval of the bank. Quite simply you cannot get your own money. I don't know what it's like in the Netherlands but, for example, in Serbia, if you forget your pin code and if you type in the wrong number three times, the cash dispenser just takes your card. Matching is a method that means that, on the basis of some information that I call a key, from one source of data, you will match the data from another source. In order to do that, you have to see what the key is. You will have to assign all of this a key. This key consists of several elements. It can be a numerical key, and it can contain certain numbers like pin codes do, for cash dispensers. But if you're not a position to give a numerical key which is the case in these reports, these matchings, then you combine that key or rather you a combination that will, with a high degree of probability, guarantee that you are going to match the same kind of units. What does that mean? If you have one's exact name, father's name and last name and, for example, a correct date of birth, when I say date of birth that is the day, month and year of birth and if that is your key for matching, then the unit thanks contain the name, last name, father's name, date of birth that you release from one source, say, the Red Cross, Red Cross files, and then if you match that with the census, then you will get the same individuals that have identical details. That would be an ideal matching process. In order to carry out this process of matching, you have to have the right information. If you do not have the right information, then you have to adjust the key. However, in scientific statistics, the method is as follows. You are the safest if you use the same key throughout the matching process because the very moment have you to change your key, depending on which elements you're changing, you are give yourself a certain freedom to target something. That's what I meant when I said targeted information. If the matching does not work the first time, the exact name, surname, father's name, date of birth, I can change the key and I can say, no, don't give me all of that, don't give me the date. Just give me the name, father's name, and the year of birth, without the actual date. And then I run it again. And I see what happens. Since I'm changing the key and then say I'm not satisfied with that either. Then I use a criteria that's even looser. And then I say don't give the full name, the full surname, the full father's name, give me the initials. For instance, the initials of the name, surname and father's name and I'm going to, say, work with an algorithm for the date of birth. Now what does that mean? That means setting certain rules that have to be observed. In order to be clear, perhaps I should say that there is an algorithm for tea making. For instance, you set a rule, saying if tea is supposed to be proper, then water has to boil and then have you to put, say, a spoonful of tea into a cup and so on and so forth. So there's also an algorithm of years that you have to work out. Usually you give a range of years, that is to say, for example, Svetlana D. Radovanovic who may be born, say, from 1946 until 1956 or say until 1952, you gave any range you want. Then they look for all the S. Radovanovics that were born in 1947, 1948 and so on and so forth, the numbers that you provided for this algorithm. And, of course, if there is S. Radovanovic then, of course, there are a lot more people that are found and you don't exactly get to me, do you? Now, when a certain number of units are matched on the basis of this criterion, then the expert has to assess, decide, on the basis of a visual method as they call it, they have it decide on the basis of some other elements that need not necessarily be contained in all the documents, whether that is precisely the Svetlana Radovanovic who is on the Red Cross list or on the list of the Srebrenica victims or the list of refugees, displaced persons, and so on and so forth. Now what is the problem here with the Prosecution experts. They give 73 possibilities for matching. The first time, they show, for example, how they match Red Cross lists and PHR lists, the first time. The first time in terms of all the reports they wrote. They never gave the statistics for matching, but now this last report, there are some absolute numbers that are given, then there can be a certain statistics of matching so the method of matching applied by the Prosecution experts was modified in a way which would satisfy what was that they were looking for. Now why are they unfair? They are unfair, they are not being intellectually honest because they could have said the following: According to criterion 1, the first time they did it, I matched such and such a number. Criterion 2, such and such a number. And within 71 criteria, they have 45, if I'm not mistaken - it can be checked - 45 criteria that are an algorithm of the year of birth, the possible place of birth and the place of permanent residence. So that is what I was speaking about in the beginning, the modification of the standard method that is used in statistics.
